items.title: Denny Zeitlin interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

ctx.x: Um hum. There actually was a whole decade that I was immersed in a kind of a multiple keyboard integration of classical, rock, jazz, funk and electronic music. It started in the late 60s, around ’67, ’68. Well before there were any kind of polyphonic synthesizers around or even portable monophonic ones. It was maybe just as the ARP 2600 was coming out. Mainly it was Moog synthesizers with patch cords and stuff. And I got engineers to build me modules and things and ring modulators. And I gradually put together a…

Right. And so Patrick and I have known each other for a long time. In the 60s he was the guy who first told me to take this cord and plug it here when I wanted to learn what a Moog synthesizer was about. So we’re doing a project together, just totally on spec which is kind of a piano concerto orchestral format where the orchestra is synthesized. And we’re having a ball. It’s my first big foray back into electronics in many years.
